=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh
  Line or code reference: 1752
  Problem: The safety check uses `if ! bash "${WORKSPACE_SAFETY_CHECK_HELPER}"; then _codex_exit=$?`. In bash, `!` inverts the exit status of the pipeline. When `workspace_safety_check.sh` exits 78, the `!` makes the conditional expression evaluate to true (exit 0), and `$?` captures 0 not 78. The later guard at line 1791 `if [ "${_codex_exit}" -eq 78 ]` will never match, so the resolver proceeds to launch Codex after a safety violation.
  Why it fails at runtime: A workspace-safety-violation (e.g. escaped workspace root) exits 78 from the helper but the resolver loop treats it as success and continues to the Codex launch block inside the else branch, defeating the entire safety invariant for the conflict-resolver path.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: tests/test_workspace_safety_check.py
  Line or code reference: 166-170
  Problem: `main()` calls only `test_helper_script_exists_and_is_executable()` and returns 0. The file defines 11 test functions but the remaining 10 (covering workspace root escape, invalid key, pwd mismatch, the no-op path, and all workflow integration assertions) are never executed when the file is run directly with `python3 tests/test_workspace_safety_check.py`.
  Why it fails at runtime: Running the test suite produces a false-pass. The violation paths, gated no-op behavior, and workflow integration checks are all defined but inert. CI or manual invocation of the test file will report success while exercising none of the safety-invariant logic.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: 434-end (413 lines deleted)
  Problem: The PR removes `_memory_force_tick_remote_url`, `_memory_force_tick_remote_branch_exists`, `_memory_force_tick_ensure_branch`, `_memory_force_tick_collision_wrapper`, `memory_force_tick_get`, and `memory_force_tick_put`. `scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh` still calls `memory_force_tick_get` and `memory_force_tick_put` at lines 335-443 using `declare -F` guards. While the guards prevent command-not-found crashes (the calls silently no-op), the cooldown mechanism that prevents the poller from dispatching duplicate force-ticks within a configurable window is entirely lost.
  Why it fails at runtime: A consumer repo that previously relied on force-tick cooldown (via `FORCE_TICK_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`) will now dispatch duplicate orchestrator ticks on every poll cycle that reaches the force-tick path, increasing GitHub API consumption and risking redundant workflow runs.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

The violation tests (`test_helper_rejects_workspace_root_escape`, `test_helper_rejects_invalid_workspace_key`, `test_helper_rejects_pwd_mismatch`), the no-op path test (`test_helper_is_noop_when_workspace_reuse_is_disabled`), the valid-path test (`test_helper_accepts_valid_reused_workspace`), and all five workflow-integration assertion tests are defined but never called.
